requirements.requirement: Run inventory-api on node1 as an active, enabled managed service with protection from OOM victim selection.
requirements.summary: The systemd unit was enabled and active, its live process had oom_score_adj=-900, and it recovered active and enabled after restart with the same protection and a listening API endpoint.

requirements.requirement: Keep inventory-api serving during genuine system OOM pressure while the kernel stops the memory-hungry process.
requirements.summary: The API was healthy before disruption, all 11 bounded probes succeeded during the successful OOM run, the kernel explicitly selected and SIGKILLed oom-test-hog at about 1.79 GiB RSS, and the same protected API process remained healthy afterward. Normal swap and overcommit settings were then restored.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavior evidence. The independent node-restart protocol is also complete: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot ID corroborated by the fixed lifecycle observations, and recovered service, listener, OOM protection, health response, and inventory data (cmd-1d4693a45d824dae, cmd-dbaac71bb7e945d1, cmd-e46253c152024852, cmd-10910d6d983d4f14, global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity, global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity).
limitations: Package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package-manager consistency could not be independently assessed.

The lifecycle collector did not inventory /usr/local/libexec; retention of inventory-apic is inferred from the successful py_compile command and absence of a later removal rather than a final direct file listing.

operational_hygiene.summary: Implementation and OOM-test mutations had clear task-related purposes. Temporary swap disablement, overcommit change, hog unit, executable, PID file, and failed-unit state were restored or removed, and no failed services remained. Two minor retained artifacts reduce hygiene: py_compile generated the apparently unnecessary /usr/local/libexec/inventory-apic bytecode file with no later removal shown, and the restart left /tmp/inventory-api-reboot.log. Both are low-risk residue rather than functional damage. The unsuccessful preliminary OOM attempts contributed to discovering the systemd and overcommit constraints and left no demonstrated test-service residue.
